rst31-v2-r2-cook-q001.objective: Remove unwanted parts and cut for the dish.
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q001.stem: Which preparation shapes an ingredient for the dish?
options: Peeling makes cutting unrelated to the dish
Always keep inedible parts
Use the same size for every dish
Remove unwanted parts and peel as needed, then cut to an edible, suitable shape
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q001.explanation: Preparation includes removal, peeling and cutting suited to the dish.
reasons: Peeling and suitable cutting require separate checks
Keeping unwanted parts is not the purpose
Required shape and size depend on the dish
It matches removal and cutting to the purpose

rst31-v2-r2-cook-q002.objective: Prepare ingredients promptly after refrigerated storage.
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q002.stem: The required ingredients have been taken from the refrigerator. What next?
options: Proceed promptly with preparation and avoid unnecessary standing
Leave them at room temperature for a long time
Ignore time if appearance is normal
Take everything out early and leave it if busy
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q002.explanation: Prepare removed ingredients promptly. Appearance alone is insufficient; prevent bacterial growth during work.
reasons: It avoids unnecessary standing through prompt preparation
Long standing conflicts with prompt work
Normal appearance does not remove time control
Plan quantity and progress without increasing standing time

rst31-v2-r2-cook-q003.objective: Distinguish washing ingredients from necessary disinfection.
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q003.stem: Which preparation reduces mud, dirt, microbes and foreign objects on ingredients?
options: Check smell without washing
Do not inspect ingredients because utensils were washed
Water alone always makes everything sterile
Wash appropriately and disinfect by the specified method when necessary
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q003.explanation: Wash ingredients properly and use specified disinfection when necessary. Washing and disinfection are different.
reasons: Smell does not replace washing
Utensils and ingredients each need appropriate handling
Water alone does not guarantee sterility
It distinguishes washing from required disinfection

rst31-v2-r2-cook-q004.objective: Choose suitable thawing that prevents bacterial growth.
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q004.stem: How should frozen ingredients be thawed according to the source?
options: Prevent growth and choose food-suitable methods such as refrigerator or running-water thawing
Prefer long standing in a warm place
Assume bacteria cannot grow during thawing
Choose from outer color alone
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q004.explanation: Prevent growth during thawing. Refrigerator and running water are examples; check conditions suitable for the food.
reasons: It connects growth prevention with a suitable method
Do not prefer long warm standing
Time and temperature matter during thawing
Color alone cannot identify a suitable method

rst31-v2-r2-cook-q005.objective: Separate one worker’s preparation, cooking and plating.
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q005.stem: Work surfaces are separated by use. May one person prepare raw ingredients, cook and plate at the same time?
options: Yes, if gloves are worn
Do not work simultaneously; finish each task and verify cleanliness before switching
Yes, if the surfaces differ
Yes, if no dirt is visible
rst31-v2-r2-cook-q005.explanation: Separate the person’s tasks as well as surfaces to prevent contamination between raw ingredients and finished food.
reasons: Gloves do not replace task separation
It avoids simultaneous work and enables a clean switch
Separate surfaces alone do not permit simultaneous work
Visible dirt alone is insufficient
